Method of Attack: DLL hijacking via Windows 10 WordPad executable (write.exe) by placing a malicious edputil.dll in the same folder as a renamed WordPad executable (document.exe), which loads the malicious DLL instead of the legitimate one
Use of curl.exe to download a DLL disguised as a PNG file from a remote host
Execution of the downloaded DLL using rundll32.exe
Stealing emails for further phishing attacks
Downloading additional payloads such as Cobalt Strike for post-exploitation
Lateral movement within corporate networks leading to data theft and ransomware attacks
Attack Vector: Phishing campaign with emails containing links to download a ZIP archive
ZIP archive contains renamed WordPad executable (document.exe) and malicious DLL (edputil.dll)
Execution of document.exe triggers DLL hijacking
Indicators of Compromise: Downloaded DLL disguised as default.png executed via rundll32.exe with command: rundll32 c:\users\public\default.png,print
